title: Add athena land --pr with opt-in REST merge, no stray emails
summary: Retry of the `athena land --pr` slice: push the job's branch, open the PR, wait for green checks, using only `gh api` (REST). The merge call is made only when a new opt-in setting (default off) is on. Otherwise Athena stops at an open, green PR and later lands the job by observing the merge with the existing merged-content check. No email address outside the allow-list appears in any file.

defaults_applied.how: All new code is Rust. gh is called as an external program and no scripts are added.
Fake-host unit tests cover the setting off and on, red checks, push refusal and the merged-content outcomes.
One focused slice: the command, the REST client and the setting. Stealth mode is left out.
No email addresses outside the allow-list, and no tokens or credentials in fixtures.
The merge gate is a code-level setting check with tests, not prose.
Reuse the installed `gh` CLI rather than adding a GitHub HTTP crate.
The verifier runs fmt, clippy and tests.

assumptions: The accepted correction is the one in the request: the merge is gated on an opt-in setting that is off by default. I could not read the earlier job's record, so I take this wording as the whole correction.
The earlier failure was an email-like literal in gh.rs, probably in a test fixture or a git author string. The retry avoids any email-shaped text.
The setting lives in the user-facing config parsed by crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, with a serde default of false, so athena.toml (a governance file) need not change.
Tests use fakes behind the existing Host and Content traits, so the network is never touched. The `gh` binary is invoked only through a thin command-runner trait.
The default path ends at an open, green PR. Landing is recorded on a later observation, which reuses `check_merged` and `apply_outcome` from pr.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: `athena land --pr <job>` exists in the CLI. It pushes only the job's work branch (through `check_push`, never forced), opens a PR, reads check status, and stores a `PrLink` in the job's state directory.
The host client in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs runs only `gh api` REST calls (paths like repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls). It has no `gh pr` subcommands, no `graphql` endpoint, and no GraphQL query text.
A new boolean setting enables merging via REST. It defaults to false when absent from the config. athena.toml is not changed, or if it is, the criterion naming it says why.

Run `cargo test`. A test with a fake host shows that with the setting off (the default) no merge request is issued and the command ends with an open, green PR. A second test shows that with the setting on the REST merge call is issued.

Run `cargo test`. A test shows that when the PR is later seen merged, `check_merged` runs and the job is landed on a matching fingerprint, or `merged-unverified` otherwise. The merged commit is found by PR number, never by reading trailers.
Run `cargo test`. A test shows that red or pending checks never trigger a merge, even with the setting on.

No email address outside the `email_allow` list in athena.toml appears in any changed file, including tests and fixtures. Use `noreply@`, `@example.com` or similar, or avoid emails entirely, e.g. no `user@host` strings in gh.rs.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. All pass.

out_of_scope: Stealth mode and PRs in repositories Athena does not own.
Any GraphQL use, including `gh pr merge --auto` and other `gh pr` subcommands.
Changes to the email allow-list or other governance files.
departures: Cost and time are above the reference. This slice adds a new module, a CLI command and a config setting, and the earlier attempt was refused at admission. Pass probability is slightly lower because new code that handles emails and network fakes is easy to get wrong.
